notes.title: DEVBLOG #11 - The future of Homebrew (part 5)
notes.content:
As much as Danny and Joe love their dome they've had expansion plans for a while and therefore the entire dome area is redesigned in the upcoming update. At last Danny will get the polished sign that he always wanted!

[img]http://i.imgur.com/0gzn03S.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]New home = new dome[/b][/h1]

The new update will allow you to build bigger vehicles faster. Therefore the dome has been entirely reworked so that you can benefit from the incoming light while having all the space you need to bring your crazy inventions to life.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/yUZa8Ry.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Helipad[/b][/h1]

Another new thing that you'll discover is the 25 m² helipad that makes landing a lot easier. Just as with the dome it's been designed with functionality in mind and it hosts a tunnel that can be used both as shelter against incoming attacks or as a shortcut to the construction zone. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/WhGwBoD.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Landing strip[/b][/h1]

A landing strip near the dome has been requested a lot and it was high on our priority list. Therefore the new valley (The Bridge) has a 200 m long runway that leads directly to the valley. At the same time it'll be equipped with lights to make landing at night easier.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/d5oPmDX.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Work in progress[/b][/h1]

A lot of work has already been done and new content is added daily. There's always room for improvement and some polishing. Therefore please keep in mind that the things that are discussed development blog represent a work in progress. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/9ZboCbd.jpg[/img]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #10 - SteamAPI
notes.content:
We've been hard at work on a lot of features lately, one of which is integration of the SteamAPI using steamworks.NET.
We've tried integrating this in the past, but always encountered issues.

So we decided to do some more testing, and we made a small test platform to test out all the things we needed. (this took no time at all with the new and improved Unity UI)

[img]http://i.imgur.com/AG6glvl.png[/img]
It took a while to get used to the way Steamworks [b]works[/b], but we've done it!
(for those familiar with coding. Think CallBacks and CallResults. On everything SteamAPI.) 

We are now able to start a lobby, fill it with server information (public IP address, port, servername, etc.), and retrieve the information using an invite! (through the steam overlay)
Why using lobbies and not Steam's Master-Servers? Well for one, your IP wont be publicly shared all over steam. Second, you can't call these lobbies, without an invitation. 

This is only the start though! As we have a lot of interesting features planned with the API. But, now that inviting people to a lobby is working (currently only in-game though.) we can start experimenting on other features (like achievements, stat-collection, how the workshop works, etc...) that can become pretty interesting.

Some people might've noticed an extra option when launching Homebrew the past couple of days.
[img]http://i.imgur.com/TL4yLpY.png[/img]

This was to test the platform out, with the steam overlay, and correct business. Without doing weird stuff to our Steam-clients.

[h1][i]So, How does it work?[/i][/h1]
Well, if you start up a server, Homebrew will start a lobby in the background. 
It'll then insert relevant server information into that lobby, like server-ip:port, password, server-name, etc.
Then the user can call the overlay for inviting people to join his server.
(Users wont be able to access the lobby without an invitation though!) 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/sVLBekj.png[/img]

After the friend accepts, they'll join the lobby ([u]this is not the actual server![/u]) in Homebrew, load the server-information, and connect using the data just like you normally would via Direct-IP (or server-list). 
[u]Be Aware[/u]: your server still needs to be [u]PORT FORWARDED[/u]! For joining the lobby it doesn't, since it creates those lobbies on Steam's side. Not on your machine. 


This might sound a bit over-complicated for what it is, but it's by far the most reliable and quickest way (without needing to rewrite our netcode)
What we'll be able to do onward now that the entire system is working however, will open up a lot of possibilities. 

[u]This is not in Homebrew V13 [i]YET[/i], but will be soon![/u]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #9 - The future of Homebrew (part 4)
notes.content:
A couple of days ago a year had passed since Homebrew got greenlit on Steam. This year has been extremely exciting and the feedback that we gathered so far is crucial for the direction that Homebrew is heading in. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/P4qJHBs.jpg[/img]


[h1][b]Transition to alpha[/b][/h1]
We've been very active on the forums, talked to the community and made lists of things that you guys want to see in-game. While at first the upcoming update was supposed to focus mainly on the UI we discovered that with our new methods/tools allowed us to fix most of the bugs and make more optimized/futureproof systems at the same time.

Right now our team is doing an amazing job on the "bigger" update that will take Homebrew from a pre-alpha state to an alpha state. This means that a lot of changes are being made to almost every part of Homebrew, the changes include, but are not limited to: code, UI, level, assets, builder mechanics, player behavior, ...

[h1][b]A first glance on the update by sk116 (a.k.a. shawnkiller90)[/b][/h1]
sk116 recently made a three part video series to show some of the things that you can expect in the new update. He's been very supportive, helped us out with testing, gave us constructive criticism and we can't thank him enough for that.

If an image's worth a thousand words then these videos are worth a lot more. Therefore we advise you to check them out for more information about the basics of the new UI, browser, builder mechanics, new tools, basic player behavior, water, skybox, the new site and more.

Please keep in mind however that most of the things that you'll see are still under development and therefore subject to change. 

[h1]Part 1[/h1]
[b]Main topics:[/b] basic UI, builder mechanic basics, some new tools, ...

[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kO9hkjcv74s[/url]
[h1]Part 2[/h1]
[b]Main topics:[/b]environment (OMENS NEST, clouds, skybox, ...), basic player behavior, ...

[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ChPVXDKUkQY[/url]
[h1]Part 3[/h1]
[b]Main topics:[/b]new site, forums, profiles (social), chatbox, steam linking, ...

[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XxEp9kYzLFE[/url]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #8 - The future of Homebrew (part 3)
notes.content:
We want to give Homebrew a fresh look to get it right and make sure that we improve both the experience and performance. In order to fix some of bugs/issues that you guys discovered some stuff needs to be replaced by something more future-proof. 

[h1][b]A new home[/b][/h1]

We mentioned in an earlier post that we've been pushing the limits of our tools, systems and Unity 5 in order to improve both graphics and performance. As of today we'd like to announce that with the bigger update, the current valley will be replaced by a better looking one. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/q8Ryy56.jpg[/img]

As development continues we'll be adding multiple areas and islands like the one we already showed (see: [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/325420/announcements/detail/225517692776751143]OMENS NEST[/url]). Because the valley is an important part of Homebrew and the islands will be located around it, we think that "THE BRIDGE" is an appropriate name. 

[h1][b]New possibilities[/b][/h1]

Based on our experience from previous level designs we learned a lot about what we should and more importantly shouldn't do. Since we have been pushing the limits of Unity 5 and our systems for quite a while now we also gained a better understanding on how far we can go.

In order to build a level that's not just good but also suits the needs of the players a crucial amount of feedback is required. We missed it in earlier stages of development, but this drastically changed after our launch as you guys have been very supportive and gave us a lot suggestions.

With this and known issues in mind our main level and model designer Marked Dog works at an amazing pace to create this new, more player friendly environment where you can test your creations to the limit.

Make sure to keep an eye out as we'll be posting more on how "The Bridge" will look and what else you can expect once the bigger update rolls out. If you have any suggestions, let us know and we'll see what can be done.

notes.title: Quick patch 22/04/'15
notes.content:
While working on the bigger update we decided to make some changes and fix some issues of the current build.

[h1][b]Helicopter rotorblades[/b][/h1]

Rotorblades now can use throttle up, throttle down and/or an axis:
This means that you'll be able to raise and lower the static RPM of the rotorblade and then increase/decrease this RPM with the axis.

You can adjust stabilizing_effect property to have more/less stabilizing force form a helicopter rotorblade[list]
[*]a value of 1 will make the rotorblade behave as normally expected 
[*]a value of 0 will make the rotor behave like a plane propeller
[/list]
[h1][b]Steer_speed property[/b][/h1]

This new property allows you to determine how fast the wheel will turn:[list]
[*]a value of 1 = maximum turning speed
[*]a value of 0 = minimal turning speed
[/list]
[h1][b]Wings[/b][/h1]

Wings now can handle 2 inputs at the same time which means that you can now hookup AxisA AND AxisB and blend them together. This will certainly come in handy when you attempt to build flying winged planes ([url=http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_wing]tailless fixed wing aircraft[/url])

[h1][b]Other fixes[/b][/h1][list]
[*]Added full-screen support for monitors
[*]Changed jet engine weight (both small and big) so that it's more accurate
[*]Curve/sphere plates convex collider: fixed collision with terrain
[*]Corrected the misaligned flap of the tapered vertical stunt plane wing
[*]Fixed hovercraft propeller invert input property
[*]Fixed autorefresh for the server list
[*]Fixed load game problems
[/list]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #7 - The future of Homebrew (part 2)
notes.content:
We noticed that a lot of you guys want to build bigger vehicles. Because we'll be expanding the world of Homebrew in the future, bigger vehicles will certainly be necessary and therefore we'd like to introduce 'construction zones'.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/4bQIwzE.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Construction zones?[/b][/h1]

While they look better than the current workshop the main benefits aren't the looks, it's the fact that building happens in an open environment rather than in a confined area. This means that you'll have plenty of room to experiment in and that it'll be accessible more easily .

[img]http://i.imgur.com/qj6izZ0.jpg[/img]

These zones are still a work in progress and they'll contain the necessary tools and systems that we've redesigned to work more efficiently and feel more intuitive at the same time. As time goes on and more islands/areas are added, more construction zones will follow accordingly.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/39b5wsv.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Update - Multiplayer Fixes!
notes.content:
We've released a small update that fixed a couple of MP bugs people have been noticing with the past update.
Some of these fixes are
[list]
[*]Vehicle Hanging and disappearing.
[*]Sending in-correct response, resulting in a "vehicle-stuck" issue.
[*]Switching to 123 no lag for me while in a vehicle would sometimes crash the player.
[*]Vehicle Names MP-Mixup bug. 
[/list]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #6 - The future of Homebrew (part 1)
notes.content:
In an earlier post we mentioned that we're preparing Homebrew for the future and that we'd start talking about it once the time was right. There's a lot of new stuff to be shown so as of today we'll be giving sneak peeks into what you can expect once the bigger update is out.
[url=http://i.imgur.com/Bwioj2g.jpg]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/Bwioj2g.jpg[/img]
[/url]
[h1][b]New possibilities[/b][/h1]

Right now Homebrew is evolving and still in early stages of development. During the last couple of weeks we designed new systems, worked with new tools and migrated to Unity 5. After testing a lot it looks like we'll be able to have better graphics and fix a lot of issues at the same time. 
[url=http://i.imgur.com/S8o6zlv.jpg]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/S8o6zlv.jpg[/img]
[/url]
[h1][b]Bringing the world alive[/b][/h1]

Our goal is to reduce level loading as much as possible. At the same time we want to have a world that feels more alive which means that a real-time day and night cycle had to be added (to view a full-sized webm click  [url=http://homebrewgame.com/wp-content/images/timelapse.webm]HERE[/url]).

[img]http://i.imgur.com/vXQLmV4.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Exploring Homebrew[/b][/h1]

While building vehicles is important, exploring the world results in countless hours of fun and we want to enhance this experience. This will be done with a totally reworked valley and as time goes on more and more islands like this one will be added.
[url=http://i.imgur.com/hIOrG1R.jpg]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/hIOrG1R.jpg[/img]
[/url]

Having these new locations will not only open up a lot of possibilities, it'll also allow us to prepare the world for new kinds of vehicles with a wider range. To make this aspect more interesting we'll be focusing on both above and below sea-level exploration.

[h1][b]Results at high settings[/b][/h1]

While the following screenshot certainly looks better than the current level, we designed our systems in a way that it'll also result in higher FPS than before. So far there's no need to worry if Homebrew will work on your current gear after the update and we want to keep it like that!

[url=http://i.imgur.com/wTiCTFy.jpg]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/wTiCTFy.jpg[/img]
[/url]
Homebrew means a lot to us and we'd never get to this point without you. Thank you guys for supporting us so far, it's truly amazing to see something that started out as a project for us and our friends turn into a way of expressing how we think about games and other things in general.

notes.title: UPDATE 13/03/2015 - Multiplayer fixes
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/H1BQLnr.jpg[/img]

After the latest update there were some issues with multiplayer. Therefore we decided to ensure that some of them are resolved by making additional changes.

[h1][b]Main changes[/b][/h1]
To resolve the most common problems we decided that it is best to eliminate direct vehicle transfer between players. This means that when you spawn a vehicle, it'll be uploaded to our server before it is passed on to other players.

You'll also notice that your vehicles will disappear every time a new player joins the server. We did this to ensure that nobody receives outdated data and we hope to have an update with a fix for this somewhere next week.

[h1]Connecting to a server[/h1]
[list]
[*]Click on Party in the main menu
[*]Click on Browse
[*]Click on the search icon to find the existing servers
[*]Select the server you want to join and enter the password (if any)
[*]Click on Join
[/list]
To connect via LAN make sure you're signed in and follow these steps:
[list]
[*]Click on Party in the main menu
[*]Click on Browse
[*]Fill in the IP-address of the host under direct join 
[*]Click on Join
[/list]
[h1]Hosting a server[/h1]
In some cases hosting a server will require port-forwarding, if you're new to this, make sure to visit [url=http://portforward.com/]this site[/url].
[list]
[*]Click on Party in the main menu
[*]Click on Host 
[*]Choose the desired settings 
[*]Click on Host
[/list]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/Qjyhhn2.jpg[/img]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #5 - Vehicles through servers (Multiplayer fixes)
notes.content:
Some of you have probably experienced issues with multiplayer after the latest update. We are aware of them and we devoted our time towards solving some of the most common ones.

[h1][b]Vehicles through server[/b][/h1]
In the past every time a vehicle was spawned, data had to be sent directly to the other players. This data transfer didn't always go as planned and in some cases people couldn't get in their vehicles, the server had to be re-hosted and so on.

Recently we decided to make additional changes and send the vehicles through our server first. Instead of direct data transfers between players, the vehicles are uploaded to our servers and then passed on.

This approach is more reliable than direct transfer because it'll fix some of the most common issues. On the other hand once a vehicle has been spawned re-uploading it won't be necessary and therefore less data has to be sent.

[h1][b]Connecting[/b][/h1]
The update won't change anything about the way that you have to connect. Hosting a server still will require port forwarding in some cases whilst joining one won't.

[h1][b]Additional multiplayer update next week[/b][/h1]
One of the things you'll notice is the fact that your vehicles will disappear every time someone joins a server meaning that you'll have to respawn. We made it this way for now to ensure that nobody receives outdated data and it's something that we hope to eliminate in the next couple of days so that an additional update can be released somewhere next week.

[h1][b]Aluminium plate set [/b][/h1]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #2 - Mirage G8 parts
notes.content:
Soon it will be spring and we agree with the comments that the snow has been in-game for too long.Therefore the upcoming update will be snow free again! 

[h1][b]Mirage G8?[/b][/h1]

The Mirage G was a two-seat twin engine prototype that was developed in the sixties in France by the Dassault Aviation company to work as a multi-role jet fighter that could be used for both interception and nuclear strike missions.

For more information, make sure to visit [url=http://www.dassault-aviation.com/en/passion/aircraft/military-dassault-aircraft/mirage-g/]Dassault's website[/url]. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/fo1YiSs.jpg[/img]

The full set contains the following parts:[list]
[*]Mirage G8 swept wing
[*]Mirage G8 tail wing
[*]Mirage G8 vertical tail wing
[*]Mirage nose
[/list]
[h1][b]Why these parts?[/b][/h1]

The Mirage G8 is a classic and we just couldn't resist it. The most interesting part is the fact that the set includes swept wings. After having tested them for a while we can't wait to see some of the crazy things that will be created with them.

The swept wing basically has two states that it can be in; for example -15° and 45°. Once you've set the states you can change the input and the time it takes to switch between both states. 

[h1]STATE I - REAR[/h1]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/WqCYi2m.jpg[/img]

[h1]STATE II - FRONT[/h1]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/BaQtzua.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Mass label[/b][/h1]

We went through some of our earlier creations and thought that it'd be fun if there was a way to see their mass. That's why we've added a mass label that you can find next to the center of gravity on all your vehicles while you're in the tuning area.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/zP6cpx5.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Summary[/b][/h1]

While the Mirage G8 parts aren't the only ones that will be released in the new update, we really think that they have a lot of potential and that they'll make a fine addition to our collection (oh and make sure to check out this amazing [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E98hUtl4mNM]podracer[/url] that Vq.I Count Squashula designed).

More information about new parts + changes will be available tomorrow.

notes.title: DEVBLOG #1
notes.content:
We're happy to see that you guys want to be more involved in the development process and that you'd like to know more about what direction we're heading in. Homebrew started out a while ago as a project for us and our friends and back then none of us could imagine that it would be the first game that we'd officially release, let alone that it would be on Early Access and that we'd have this community on such short notice. 

Thanks for all the feedback and suggestions you've given us so far and most of all for ensuring that we can continue development.

Like promised, we're working on making it a habit to share more information on the things that we're working on. This doesn't mean that we won't be active on the forums and chat anymore, so if you have suggestions or encounter issues you can contact us at any moment!

[h1][b]What are we working on?[/b][/h1]

The main reason why Homebrew is called a pre-alpha is because there's a lot of stuff that we want to add and there are some outdated systems that need to be replaced by cleaner and better ones. 

A while ago we succesfully migrated from Unity 4 to Unity 5 and started cleaning up our code. It's still a work in progress but we don't want to rely on things that will slow us down in the long run and cause some of the bigger bugs (like vehicle corruption for example). 

Cleaner and more optimized systems is a start, but we're working on the visual aspects as well. We gave Unity 5 a hard time by pushing its limits each day and have a better understanding of the opportunities and possible pitfalls that it holds for us.

You'll be able to read more on this topic in the following posts days/weeks.

[h1][b]Update[/b][/h1]

notes.title: DEVBLOG #1
notes.content:
We're happy to see that you guys want to be more involved in the development process and that you'd like to know more about what direction we're heading in. Homebrew started out a while ago as a project for us and our friends and back then none of us could imagine that it would be the first game that we'd officially release, let alone that it would be on Early Access and that we'd have this community on such short notice. 

Thanks for all the feedback and suggestions you've given us so far and most of all for ensuring that we can continue development.

Like promised, we're working on making it a habit to share more information on the things that we're working on. This doesn't mean that we won't be active on the forums and chat anymore, so if you have suggestions or encounter issues you can contact us at any moment!

[h1][b]What are we working on?[/b][/h1]

The main reason why Homebrew is called a pre-alpha is because there's a lot of stuff that we want to add and there are some outdated systems that need to be replaced by cleaner and better ones. 

A while ago we succesfully migrated from Unity 4 to Unity 5 and started cleaning up our code. It's still a work in progress but we don't want to rely on things that will slow us down in the long run and cause some of the bigger bugs (like vehicle corruption for example). 

Cleaner and more optimized systems is a start, but we're working on the visual aspects as well. We gave Unity 5 a hard time by pushing its limits each day and have a better understanding of the opportunities and possible pitfalls that it holds for us.

You'll be able to read more on this topic in the following posts days/weeks.

[h1][b]Update[/b][/h1]

Right now we're prepping up the snow removal update. This took us a bit longer than expected due to additional changes but it'll be out in a matter of days. You'll be able to read more about them tomorrow.

notes.title: Update : More Armor parts!
notes.content:
We've added new armor platings! and decreased the amount of weight of every plating. 

We've added a 9x9 sized armor plate, a 9x9 sized curved armor plate, and a 9x9 size spherical armor plate.
The previous weight ratio was based on steel, but we felt like it was way too heavy for it's purpose, so all weights from the plating are now halved.

notes.title: UPDATE: Basic armor parts!
notes.content:
[h1][b]Basic steel armor[/b][/h1]

This update includes a few armor plates that can be used on a variety of vehicles. 

The plates are not part of the plating/skin system that we've talked about in our previous posts. For that we'll need more time to ensure that it is user friendly and contains all the necessary tools for customization.

We did get a lot of requests for parts that can be used as plating however and we've noticed an increase in vehicles where parts are used as plating. Therefore we added a few pre-made armor plates that can be found in the parts browser.

Have a look at these screenshots to get a better idea of what to expect.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/aj7EjGI.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/uKWbBTj.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/yiGSbkv.jpg[/img]

Currently the only included material is steel; it'll add weight to your creation and affect its behavior, but it will certainly protect your vital parts in combat. As you can see, the parts can be used both as 'plating' and armor at the same time. Once the final system is in place however, using them mainly for additional armor instead of cosmetics.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/SV30U7S.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/H04tiBY.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/8xzFmiA.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]New demo[/b][/h1]

As of today an up to date demo version is available on Steam. It has a bunch of new features and supports cross-play with the pre-alpha owners. Soon you'll be able to read more about the changes we've made on our [url=www.homebrewgame.com][b]website[/b][/url]

notes.title: UPDATE January 11 2015 - Optimization!
notes.content:
[h1]Big Update![/h1]
We've got a pretty big optimization update!
We completely optimized the menu, trimmed down on the trees, and did some general optimization. 
Homebrew should run a bit smoother now (especially on older rigs), and we added an option to disable water reflection (Smooths out the game a ton!). 
We've also added a couple new race tracks, and a quest marker can randomly appear on top of a random race-track. 
We also added a boat race [i]under[/i] the outer marks of the world. 

We've also made some changes in the Hangar, there's now a "More Tutorials" button on the bottom right, this'll disappear after a certain period. Clicking this will open up your browser with community video tutorials!
The pipe builder also has numbers on the grid now, as requested by some users. 


You can also paste your steam key directly into Homebrew now! (this took a bit longer then expected. Sorry guys.) 


Currently we're migrating to our new workstations, so we can work full-time on the UI update. 


[i]TL;DR[/i]

[b]Added[/b]
[list][*]Added numbers on pipe building workbench
[*]New Race tracks (Water land [i]And Air![/i] )
[*]Option to disable Reflections
[*]Paste Steam key
[*]Map changes
[/list]
[b]Fixed[/b]
[list][*]Optimized Menu
[*]Optimized Trees
[*]Optimized Map
[/list]

[i]Ps: we did more, but unfortunately we lost our bug-list. So we might update this list if we remember some other changes we made![/i]


[i]Update!: We just found another bug with Multiplayer, fix should be live now! [/i]

notes.title: Winter special update
notes.content:
Since it'll be Christmas and new year soon, we thought that this would be a great moment for an update and some gifts from us. Now let's have a look at what winter brings us this year:

[h1][b]Full sandbox mode[/b][/h1]
Like most of you probably know, the orbs were a temporary solution that  gave us some extra time to fix bugs and see how the game evolved. 

There has always been a way to get 'infinite" orbs (all praise Tesla for that), but we think that now the time is right to turn Homebrew into a full sandbox. 

Here's the stuff we changed to achieve this goal: 
[list]
[*]Removed orbs
[*]Removed warehouse
[*]Reworked world tutorial
[*]Changed save game structure
[*]...
[/list]
[h1][b]World[/b][/h1]
We were working on the optimization of the level and we started thinking about how we can give the world a more seasonal feel. Some of the changes that are listed below will remain for a long time while others (like snow for example) will be removed later on.

These are the biggest changes to the world:
[list]
[*]Changed summer theme to winter
[*]Added more roads and fixed/replaced old ones
[*]Added snow + ice
[*]Updated valley mountains
[*]Made changes inside the dome
[*]Added anti-lag level (type 123 no lag for me in chat to enable/disable it)
[*]...
[/list]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/iRjNLHY.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/Aj4B9iG.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Race tracks are here![/b][/h1]
We've added multiple race tracks that are scattered around the world. This is just a small fraction of what we have in mind for the challenge editor in the future.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/POdN3Gz.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/zzUokZL.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]New parts[/b][/h1]
We received a lot of awesome ideas from the community and this quickly resulted in a long wishlist :). We'll be releasing a lot more parts in the future and some of the suggestions will definitely be included.

Here are the parts for this update:
[list]
[*]Fireworks
[*]Burst rockets
[*]VTOL tilt rotor
[/list]

[img]http://i.imgur.com/XuXW5dO.jpg[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/WqgaFLR.jpg[/img]

[h1][b]Bug and other fixes[/b][/h1]
We're still amazed about how much feedback we've received from our community. You guys helped us find and solve bugs faster and although we're still working on some of them, Homebrew gets a bit better every day. 

Here are the fixes in this update:
[list]
[*]Fixed browning bug
[*]Fixed rename bug
[*]Fixed lights on water bug
[*]Fixed electric motor bug: reverse gear should work fine now
[*]Fixed some minor bugs
[*]Fixed some text
[*]...
[/list]

[h1][b]Meet Joe[/b][/h1]
There was one important character missing so far, it was the mechanic named Joe and he is the [i]other[/i] owner of the JOEDAN workshop. Just like Danny he has his own story to tell and you'll discover more about them further into development. 

For now however, Joe just wants to hang out and make some friends. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/GSDx31G.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/hu4o89o.png[/img]

[h1][b]Other changes[/b][/h1]
[list]
[*]Added sounds
[*]Added music
[*]Added new third person camera mode
[*]Reworked tutorial texts
[*]Added invert_input property to propellers and other
[*]You can now set tree distance to 0
[*]Made changes to the pyramid ;)
[*]Added force direction indicators
[*]Added invert property to all axis-controllable
[*]Cube scans vehicles in workshop
[*]Added new default vehicles
[*]Added new secret
[*]Optimization
[*]...
[/list]

notes.title: Winners of the boat challenge
notes.content:
Now that the polls are closed, we are glad to announce the winners of the boat challenge. 

As mentioned before the top 5 would be selected by the community and we'd pick the top 3 afterwards based on the following criteria:

- possibility to be used as a standard vehicle
- handling & functionality
- name & design

[olist]
[*][b]The Dude - The Dispatcher[/b]
In our opinion this is the boat that we were looking for! It'll need some testing before we include it as a default vehicle, but it looks like really stable and easy to tweak for beginners, ...
 
[*][b]Sicbm.com - War Boat 01[/b]
Amazing boat which shows a lot of what you can build in Homebrew if you put some effort into it. We'd love to have the vehicle for ourselves, but we think that it is just too advanced to be included as a default vehicle.

[*][b]pen4711 - Water Skipper and Xacto - Oceanis[/b]
This was one was just too difficult to choose because both boats have a lot of potential and are too different at the same time. Therefore you guys share a well deserved third place.
[/olist]

I've added all of you so that we can send you guys the keys.

We'll be doing future challenges soon, so keep an eye out on our community hub.


Cheers!

Copybugpaste Team

notes.title: [GLITCH] Hovercraft Cushions Blowers
notes.content:
[h1]Aware[/h1]
[b]HOVERCRAFT CUSHIONS[/b] have a small chance to corrupt your vehicles.
We have yet found a fix, but are working on it! 

[i]Adding a new part after your hovercraft cushion blower has been [u]LINKED[/u] to nodes, your vehicle has a small chance to get corrupted.[/i]
We have not been able to recreate this glitch with every try, so we're not sure what's the cause of it. But we're working on it.
